compatibility.title: Which Alfa Romeo Models Use the 937A4000 1.9 JTDm?
compatibility.intro: The 937A4000 is a 16‑valve evolution of the Fiat‑group JTD common‑rail diesel family, introduced in 2003 and fitted across the Alfa Romeo range. It represented a significant step up from the earlier 8‑valve JTD, offering smoother power delivery and better refinement. The engine was used in the 147, 156 and also found its way into Fiat Stilo models - a true workhorse of the early‑2000s Fiat‑group diesel lineup.

costGuide.title: Alfa Romeo 937A4000 1.9 JTDm Engine Replacement Cost (UK)
costGuide.labourLine: Fitting a 937A4000 1.9 JTDm typically takes 8-10 hours at £70-£95/hr (independent Alfa Romeo diesel specialist) - the transverse layout and common‑rail system add moderate complexity, but the engine is well‑understood with excellent parts availability across the Fiat‑group network.【PATTERN DATA】
paragraphs: The biggest price movers for a 937A4000 replacement are turbocharger condition (VNT units are more expensive to replace), injector health (common‑rail injectors require coding), and whether the timing belt and water pump have been replaced. Engines with documented cambelt service history (every 72,000 miles or 4 years) command a premium. See our full /prices/reconditioned-engine-cost guide for more detail.

failures.title: Alfa Romeo 937A4000 1.9 JTDm Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: EGR Valve Carbon Buildup - the classic JTD issue
items.whatHappens: The 937A4000's EGR valve is notorious for carbon buildup and sticking, particularly on vehicles used primarily for short urban journeys. The EGR valve actuator shaft becomes gummed up with soot and corrosion, causing it to stick - typically in the open position. Symptoms include severe lack of power, hesitation, rough idle, and the MCSF (Motor Control System Failure) warning light appearing.
items.repairVsReplace: EGR valve cleaning is a routine service item (£150-£300). If the valve has seized, replacement costs £250-£400. A blanking plate can be fitted (common on enthusiast cars), though this is not road‑legal for UK use. Read our full /failures/egr-valve-failure guide

items.title: Common‑Rail Injector Wear - the Bosch solenoid units
items.whatHappens: The 937A4000 uses Bosch solenoid‑type injectors (0445110010) operating at up to 1,450 bar. While prized for their mechanical simplicity and tolerance to varying fuel qualities, they can wear over time, leading to rough idle, misfires, poor starting, and excessive smoke. Failed injectors can leak back fuel to the tank, causing longer cranking times before the engine fires.
items.repairVsReplace: Injector refurbishment costs £100-£250 per injector. Replacement costs £200-£400 per injector plus coding. A full set of four reconditioned injectors with coding typically costs £800-£1,200. Read our full /failures/injector-failure guide

items.title: Variable Vane Turbocharger (VNT) Issues - sticking vanes
items.whatHappens: The 937A4000 uses a variable geometry turbocharger (VNT). Carbon buildup on the vane mechanism can cause the vanes to stick, resulting in overboost or underboost conditions. Symptoms include sudden power loss, excessive smoke, and the engine going into limp mode. In severe cases, the turbocharger can fail completely, sending debris through the engine.
items.repairVsReplace: Turbocharger cleaning or VNT mechanism service costs £400-£800. Full turbo replacement costs £800-£1,500. Regular oil changes are critical - old, degraded oil accelerates carbon buildup in the turbo. Read our full /failures/turbocharger-failure guide

items.title: Timing Belt - critical service item
items.whatHappens: The 937A4000 uses a timing belt rather than a chain. A broken timing belt will cause pistons to strike valves - catastrophic engine damage that often writes off the engine. The cambelt must be replaced at 72,000 miles or 4 years. Many specialists recommend 60,000 miles or 5 years for peace of mind.
items.repairVsReplace: Timing belt kit replacement (including tensioner, idler and water pump) costs £300-£600. If the belt has broken, the engine is almost certainly destroyed - valve damage is nearly universal.

failures.goodYearsLine: The 937A4000 1.9 JTDm was produced from 2003 to 2006, representing the 16‑valve evolution of the Fiat‑group JTD engine. It was later replaced by the higher‑output 937A5000 (150 hp) and the 192B1000 (140 hp) variants. The engine is a favourite among Alfa Romeo enthusiasts for its combination of performance and economy - with a simple remap, power can be increased to approximately 175 hp and 380 Nm without compromising reliability. The JTD family is considered one of the most durable diesel engines of its era when properly maintained.

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the 937A4000 1.9 JTDm
variants.intro: The 937A4000 is a Specific engine code - it identifies the 126 hp 16‑valve version of the 1.9 JTDm used in Alfa Romeo 147 and 156 from 2003 to 2006. Unlike Family pages that cover multiple fundamentally different engines, this page covers the 937A4000 as a single engine. It is important to distinguish it from the 937A5000 (150 hp) and other JTD variants. Where to find your engine code: The engine code is stamped on a machined pad on the engine block - typically on the front face, just below the cylinder head, or on the driver's side of the block. It also appears on the V5C registration document under "Engine number" (e.g. 937A4000xxxxxx). Use an Alfa Romeo VIN decoder to confirm the exact variant from the build sheet. Key 937A4000 variants: | Variant | Power | Torque | Key Difference | Applications | |---|---|---|---|---| | 937A4000 | 126 hp (93 kW) @ 4,000 rpm | 280-300 Nm | Bosch EDC16C39 ECU | Alfa Romeo 147, 156, Sportwagon | | 937A4000 (Stilo) | 126 hp (93 kW) | 280 Nm | Different ECU calibration | Fiat Stilo, Stilo Multi Wagon | Why fitting the wrong variant matters: While all 937A4000 engines share the same basic architecture (1,910 cc, 82.0 mm bore × 94.4 mm stroke, 18.5:1 compression ratio, Bosch EDC16C39 ECU), they have different ECU calibrations and emissions hardware depending on the application (Alfa Romeo vs Fiat). Fitting a Stilo ECU into an Alfa Romeo will result in reduced performance and potential drivability issues. Always ensure the replacement engine matches the donor vehicle's ECU and immobiliser coding. Commonly confused codes: | Engine Code | What it is | Why it's confused | |---|---|---| | 937A5000 | 150 hp (110 kW) 1.9 JTDm | Same displacement, higher tune - different ECU, turbo and injectors | | 192B1000 | 140 hp 1.9 JTDm | Different tune and ECU calibration | | 937A2000 | 1.9 JTD 8V (115-120 hp) | Same displacement, 8‑valve head - different cylinder head and valvetrain |

relatives.description: the 8‑valve version of the 1.9 JTD, fitted to earlier Alfa Romeo 147 and 156 models from 2000-2003. Producing 115-120 hp (85-88 kW), the 8‑valve was a simpler, less refined engine than the 16‑valve 937A4000. The 16‑valve head brought better breathing, smoother power delivery, and improved refinement - a significant step forward for the JTD family.

the 150 hp (110 kW) 1.9 JTDm that replaced the 937A4000 in the Alfa Romeo 147 and 156 from 2005 onward. Features a different turbocharger, higher boost pressure, and revised ECU calibration to deliver 150 hp and 305 Nm torque. The 937A5000 is a direct evolution of the 937A4000 and shares the same basic architecture - many components are interchangeable.

relatives.code: Fiat Stilo 1.9 JTD 16V: The same 937A4000 engine fitted to the Fiat Stilo and Stilo Multi Wagon (2003-2008). Mechanically identical to the Alfa Romeo version but with Fiat‑specific ECU calibration and emissions hardware. Parts are interchangeable, and many Stilo owners source components from Alfa Romeo breakers.

relatives.description: the 140 hp (103 kW) 1.9 JTDm fitted to later Fiat Stilo and Lancia Delta models. Uses the same 16‑valve head and common‑rail system but with different turbo and ECU calibration. Not a direct swap without ECU modifications.

the high‑output 1.9 JTDm used in the Alfa Romeo 147 JTDm and 159 1.9 JTDm (early models). Produces 170 hp (125 kW) and 330 Nm torque. Features a larger turbocharger, different injectors, and upgraded internals. Not a direct swap without significant modification.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement 937A4000 1.9 JTDm - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: ** A used 937A4000 can be a very cost‑effective option for lower‑value host vehicles (sub‑£2,000 147, 156) - especially given the low used engine prices starting from £750. However, only buy from a donor with documented proof of timing belt replacement (within the last 4 years/72,000 miles) and EGR/turbo health. Given the engine's known weaknesses (EGR carbon, injector wear, VNT sticking), a used unit without history is a gamble. Used prices from £750-£1,200 reflect this risk. Link once:

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: ** A properly reconditioned 937A4000 is the recommended choice for owners who plan to keep their Alfa Romeo long‑term. A full recon should address the engine's known weak points: new timing belt, tensioner, idler and water pump, new injectors (with coding), EGR valve cleaning or replacement, turbocharger inspection and VNT cleaning, new gaskets and seals throughout, and a full common‑rail system flush. Given the £1,500-£2,500 supply cost and the host vehicle value (£1,500-£4,500 for a decent 147/156), this represents a significant but justifiable investment for an enthusiast. A 12-24 month warranty is essential. Link once:

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: ** A full 937A4000 rebuild is justified for low‑mileage, well‑maintained examples or where the owner plans long‑term ownership. An upgraded rebuild should include new pistons, rings, bearings, timing belt, oil pump, and a full valvetrain refresh. Rebuild costs (£2,200-£3,500+) are significant relative to the vehicle's value - only consider this for high‑value or sentimental vehicles (e.g. rare 156 GTA‑spec, concours examples). Link once:

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: ** All supply options can be fitted through our network of vetted Alfa Romeo diesel specialists nationwide, with a minimum 12‑month warranty on reconditioned and rebuilt units and full nationwide delivery coverage. Fitting costs typically range from £700-£900. Link once:
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: ** The 937A4000 sits in ageing Italian host vehicles: Alfa Romeo 147 (£1,000-£3,500), Alfa Romeo 156 (£1,200-£4,000), and Alfa Romeo 156 Sportwagon (£1,000-£3,500)【THIRD‑PARTY - AutoTrader UK market data 2025】. A £1,500-£2,500 reconditioned unit represents 30-70%+ of the vehicle's value on many examples - on a £1,500 147, a £1,800 replacement is 120% of the vehicle's value, making it a borderline or non‑viable decision. The honest marketplace‑neutrality position is: if your 937A4000 has suffered catastrophic failure (timing belt break, turbo failure sending debris through the engine) and your vehicle is worth under £2,000, evaluate scrap or part‑exchange value before committing to a replacement. For well‑maintained, enthusiast‑owned examples with good bodywork and service history, the replacement can be a worthwhile investment - the JTD engine is a characterful and durable unit that rewards careful maintenance.【THIRD-PARTY】

items.answer: The engine code is stamped on a machined pad on the engine block (typically on the front face) and appears on the V5C under 'Engine number' - the code will read 937A4000xxxxxx, 937A5000xxxxxx or 937A6000xxxxxx. items.question: Is the 937A4000 1.9 JTDm reliable, and what mileage can I expect?
items.answer: The 937A4000 is one of the most durable diesel engines of its era, with an estimated lifespan of 150,000-200,000+ miles with proper maintenance. The JTD family is considered bulletproof when the cambelt is changed on time, EGR is regularly cleaned, and oil changes are performed every 10,000 miles using the correct specification oil. Timing belt replacement is critical - 72,000 miles or 4 years. EGR valve cleaning should be performed every 40,000-60,000 miles. Regular oil changes with the correct 5W‑40 oil are essential. The JTD engine responds well to remapping - many owners achieve 175 hp and 380 Nm with a simple tune.
